carmen: Heads up — onboarding a new HF model (hf/x-phi) and our eval suite shows a weird bump in answer drift after converting a chat_template -> Redwood prompt. Suspect conversion of consecutive instruction blocks + curly-brace escapes. Paste of original HF chat_template below:

carmen: ```jinja
{% chat %}
- role: system
  content: |-
    You are a helpful assistant.
- role: user
  content: |
    {{ instruction }}
{% endchat %}

{% chat %}
- role: user
  content: |
    Follow-up: {{ followup }}
- role: assistant
  content: |
    {% if hint %}{{ hint }}{% endif %}
{% endchat %}
```

carmen: After our conversion script it became a single prompt where the two user blocks got glued and the assistant conditional vanished in many cases. Example converted prompt (truncated):

carmen: ```text
SYSTEM: You are a helpful assistant.
USER: {{ instruction }} Follow-up: {{ followup }}
ASSISTANT:
```

mike: hmm — did the jinja renderer options change? We usually set trim_blocks and lstrip_blocks. If the template had trailing newlines the second chat block might be merged. Also check for autoescape or whitespace control like `{{-` / `-}}`.

anya: Also check tokenizer special tokens — if we didn't add a separator token between chats the model sees a single long user message. Do you have the model's config.json? Sometimes `add_special_tokens` / `special_tokens_map` differences cause missing BOS/SEP markers.

carmen: config.json excerpt I used: ```json
{"model_type": "gpt-like", "add_bos_token": false, "eos_token": "</s>"}
```

carmen: I think the HF artifact assumed the chat template runtime would insert separators; our conversion relies on explicit markers. The mismatch would explain the hallucination/regression in the eval where expected assistant context was missing.

ravi: Quick repro I ran against the tokenizer: ```py
# tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("hf/x-phi")
print(tokenizer.encode("You are a helpful assistant.\nUSER: hi\nUSER: follow-up", add_special_tokens=False))
print(tokenizer.encode("You are a helpful assistant.\nUSER: hi\n<SEP>USER: follow-up", add_special_tokens=False))
```

ravi: numbers differ and the model logits show a big jump at the point where <SEP> would be. So we need to either: (A) update conversion to inject a safe separator between consecutive user blocks, or (B) adjust config to set add_bos_token/eos/sep and teach Redwood to honor those tokens.

anya: For quick mitigation edit the conversion to insert `\n<|sep|>\n` between blocks and register that token with tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"additional_special_tokens":["<|sep|>"]}) — remember to update tokenizer config on disk so the runtime picks it up.

mike: Another gotcha: the assistant conditional `{% if hint %}` becomes empty string if hint missing, which in our conversion trimmed the whole assistant section because we collapse empty assistant segments. Don't collapse assistant nodes; emit an explicit placeholder like `ASSISTANT: <EMPTY>` so KV-cache alignment stays stable.

carmen: good call. I'll patch conversion to: 1) not collapse assistant nodes, 2) insert explicit sep token between adjacent user blocks, 3) ensure we write tokenizer.json with the extra token. I'll run eval after.

infra-bot: deploy-note: small template-conversion patch queued for staging (job 3289). If tests pass, we'll promote to canary tomorrow. :rocket: 

mike: one more note — add a unit test that renders multiple chat blocks with/without whitespace-control (`{{-` / `-}}`) and asserts separators present. That prevented regressions last time.

carmen: assigning to myself, will post results here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
